definition: Using a handful of examples inside the prompt to teach a model a task, without updating its weights.
details: GPT-3 showed that scaling alone lets a language model learn a new task from just a few demonstrations supplied as input. Few-shot examples condition the model to the desired format and behavior and remain a workhorse technique for steering models cheaply before resorting to fine-tuning.

citation.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
citation.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 33 (NeurIPS)
